class_rule: Minimum budget is the smallest tested budget passing unchanged accuracy/gain/guard gates; never if none. Do not assume monotonic recovery. Normalize clipped one-hot ridge scores for multiclass Brier; these are forecasts to test, not assumed calibrated probabilities.
class_support: Keep 2/4/8/16/never classes fixed regardless of observed support. Report zero counts, unsupported classes and constant scalar labels explicitly; never hide under-repair behind majority class accuracy.
constants: TRAIN class frequencies and per-budget TRAIN recovery prevalence/utility mean. Also evaluate fixed 2/4/8/16 and no-action policies.
evaluation: Report minimum-class accuracy/multiclass Brier and each budget recovery Brier plus utility MSE/MAE, against constants, confidence/output/frozen/tuned and all predeclared label shuffles. Always report pooled and equal-source means and per-source results; no intent bootstrap, significance tests or treating permutation draws as independent models. Separate policy differences from forecast error reduction.
failure_rule: No model or prediction work before original gate authorization. Failed fresh learning, lens qualification or fresh TRAIN class gate blocks downstream work. Preserve receipts; any changed protocol requires a new named TRAIN study. No old TEST reuse.
feature_rule: Unchanged before/after mean probe metrics and layer choices. Labels are never learner-training targets. Fit scalers on TRAIN only; all lenses use background TRAIN activations rather than predictor-cohort utterances.
fresh_train_gate: Even if the original pilot passes, require the same informative minimum-budget class distribution on fresh TRAIN outcomes before fitting any predictor or starting TEST readout/repair. Never fit a scalar binary discrimination claim from a constant label.
history_boundary: A minimum-budget response curve does not by itself identify stored-binding reuse. Matched retain-only curves at smaller budgets would be required for a recovery-speed advantage claim; the earlier 16-update references nearly saturate.

label_permutations.rule: Seal indices using all eligible fresh TRAIN units at the fresh cohort gate before repair. Fit 40 tuned-feature nulls using TRAIN-label permutations only, shared across all outcome targets. Report actual changed labels and active/inert draw counts by scheme for the minimum class, every one-hot class, per-budget binary recovery and utility. Retain inert scalar draws; no redraw.

gates.acquisition_baseline: At least .3 improvement from start of the relevant training phase: initial old-gate scores for old acquisition; acquired-checkpoint new-gate scores for later-task acquisition. Never count a pre-existing output-code bias as a newly learned binding.

learning.mechanisms: Unmodified source AdamW, rank-8 adapter, acquired and forgotten checkpoints, 128 old then 128 new updates with continuous optimizer. Old and new phase gains remain required. No silent retry or relaxed threshold.

lens.method: Reuse frozen tuned_lens.py implementation: residual affine translators, full-vocabulary forward KL, frozen norm/head/model, trained only on 512 disjoint TRAIN background prompts; validate on 128 separate TRAIN background prompts. Fit new translators at each fresh acquired checkpoint and freeze through forgetting.
lens.qualification: The original >=5% aggregate heldout KL improvement over frozen lens must pass at acquisition and also at the forgotten checkpoint before repairs. No adaptive lens training based on repair outcomes. A failed lens stops that source and its dependent study; a separate new TRAIN protocol is needed to change calibration.

minimum_budget_gate.requirement: Completed execution and passing scientific receipt; recompute the original gate from its completed TRAIN sources before authorization. A failed or incomplete gate permits no fresh learning, lens updates, predictors or TEST actions.

name: fresh-clinc-minimum-budget-prediction-20260912
policy_rule: Choose the most probable minimum class, breaking ties toward the smaller numeric budget; never maps to no action. Save choices before TEST repair. The main policy report pairs qualification fraction, updates and utility for each source, pooled and equal-source. Compare every policy with always-2, always-16 and TRAIN-majority (constant_train); retain fixed 4/8/no-action too. Any descriptive savings claim requires positive baseline qualification and no qualification loss on each heldout source. Class accuracy alone is not a policy win. Exhaustive paired-grid evaluation estimates policy behavior, not actual savings in study total updates.
predictor: Per-scalar ridge with fixed alpha 10 and TRAIN-only centering/scaling, equal intent weights. Fit 5 one-hot minimum classes (2/4/8/16/never), and per-budget recovery and continuous utility. No hyperparameter or feature selection from TEST.
repairs: Independent fresh AdamW starts at the same forgotten adapter. Same 16-step balanced schedule; evaluate 16 first while saving 2/4/8/16 checkpoints, then independently reproduce 2/4/8 prefixes exactly. 30 updates per intent. Reload checks, same 16-code test/guard rows and frozen backbone. All readouts and TEST forecasts are sealed before actions.
scope: Prospective recovery-budget prediction for bounded 16-code intent-to-code bindings. Four fresh learning streams; only two independent heldout source models. No semantic erasure, model-level J-Access replication or stored-binding reuse claim.
